entry_state: Instrument reduction retains each stopped portion's value at removal and assigns only subsequent changes outside the hedge. The same remaining nominal quantity can produce different reserve and profit when a different instrument is reduced. The next example instead stops part of the forecast purchase, which requires a different reserve history.
exit_state: Stopping a homogeneous purchase portion freezes its attached reserve while later derivative changes enter profit. Still expected, canceled and unrecoverable-loss cases have different releases. Different designation origins cannot use a total nominal fraction; the next case introduces separately matched origin gains and leaves its generalisation unfinished.
findings: The20%split requires identical per-unit exposure and common origin; it is not a generic reserve allocation rule.
